steps.title: The plan door compares against the merge base
steps.done_when: `planBoundary` reads its `before` plan from `git merge-base origin/<base> origin/<head>` and falls back to `origin/<base>` only when that cannot be read, with a test for a plan edit that landed on main after the branch started.
instruction: src/mc/merge-boundary.js, `planBoundary`: `before` is `git show origin/<base>:<path>` — main as it is now. A planning commit that lands on main after the step's branch was cut makes main differ from the head at steps the session never touched, and `unauthorisedChanges` reports them as the session's (memoro #11603, 2026-09-08: `steps[30]: changed by the session that ran step 7`, which was #11600's edit on main).

After the fetch and after `path` is known: `git merge-base origin/<base> origin/<head>`; when it exits 0 and `git show <sha>:<path>` exits 0, that text is the `before` text. When either fails — no common ancestor, or the plan did not exist at the merge base — use `origin/<base>:<path>` exactly as today. The door still fails open (`notChecked`) on the reads it fails open on now.

The byte-identical shortcut compares the chosen `before` text with the head's. `stepOfPr(after.plan, pr)` and `unauthorisedChanges(before.plan, after.plan, index)` are unchanged. The project list and `path` still come from `ls-tree origin/<base>`.

A branch that merged origin/main into itself has the merged main commit as its merge base, so main's edits up to that merge are in `before` and are not the session's — that is the intended reading, say it in the module's doc comment, and replace the comment's sentence about "a base copy that will not `git show`" so it names the fallback.

instruction: src/mc/branch-landed.js: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <branch>` exits 1 on a conflict, the helper returns null and the answer is `unknown`. `freshBranch` (src/mc/run.js, `grep -n "freshBranch"`) treats `unknown` as work and leaves the workarea on a branch that has landed; on 2026-09-11 `step-cost` step 2 ran on `step-cost-2` after #693 had landed from it, was handed a conflict on main's own later edit, and had its push refused by the push-guard at the end of the session.

`branchLanded` stays local and network-free; do not add `gh` to it. Add the second question to `freshBranch`, where the network is already used: when `branchLanded` says `unknown`, ask GitHub what the push-guard asks (`pushVerdict` in src/mc/push-guard.js asks `gh pr list --head <branch> --state merged`, but returns no head sha and is not changed here): through the `gh` seam run.js already uses for `gh pr list --head <branch> --state open`, run `gh pr list --head <branch> --state merged --limit 5 --json number,mergedAt,headRefOid`, take the newest by `mergedAt`, and if its `headRefOid` equals the branch's current tip (`git rev-parse <branch>`) the branch is landed: take the same path as `landed`. steps.title: The quota pause lasts until the reset the refusal names
steps.done_when: A quota answer whose text carries `resets …` holds every lane until one minute after that time, in slices that end on STOP or UPDATE; one without a readable time keeps the thirty minutes.
instruction: src/mc/run.js `quotaPause()` sleeps `QUOTA_SLEEP_MS` (30 min, run-plan.js:65) whatever the refusal said. On 2026-09-08 a weekly limit that reset three days later cost eight launches of `sql-w5-relationship-closure`, one every thirty minutes, each `rc=1 3s note=quota`. The refusal text carries the time. Every one of the 104 refusals in `~/mc/runner/log/` has the same form: `You've hit your weekly limit · resets Sep 11 at 3pm (Europe/Stockholm)`.

In src/mc/run-plan.js, beside `quotaSeen`, add `export function quotaResetAt(text, now = new Date())` → `Date | null`. Pattern: `resets (?:(<Mon>) (<d>) at )?(<h>)(?::(<mm>))?\s?(am|pm)(?: \((<IANA zone>)\))?`, case-insensitive, month as a three-letter English abbreviation. No date means today in that zone, or tomorrow when that time has already passed. A date earlier than `now` by more than a day means next year. No zone means the machine's. Convert zone wall time to an instant with `Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone, … }).formatToParts` — compute the zone's offset at the candidate instant and correct once; no dependency is added. An unknown zone name or anything unparseable returns null. Never return a time more than eight days after `now` — return null instead.
`parseSession` (run-plan.js, the three places that set `quota`) also returns `quotaReset: quota ? quotaResetAt(<the same text it tested>, now) : null`; the dash object carries `quotaReset: null`.

`quotaPause(until = null)` in run.js: the deadline is `until + 60 s` when `until` is a Date in the future, else `now + QUOTA_SLEEP_MS`. It sleeps in slices of `Math.min(remaining, QUOTA_SLEEP_MS)` through `deps.sleep`, and between slices returns early when `stopRequested()` or `updateRequested()` is true — a pause of days must not make the runner deaf to STOP and UPDATE. The shared `quotaSleep` promise stays one promise for all lanes. The log line says the time: `quota seen — every lane sleeping until <ISO> (the refusal's reset)` or the old thirty-minute wording. Both callers (`if (turn.quota) await quotaPause()` near line 1236 and `if (read.quota) await quotaPause()` near line 1688) pass the parsed reset. `deps.now` — use whatever clock run.js already injects (`grep -n "deps.now\|Date.now" src/mc/run.js`); if there is none, add `now: () => new Date()` to `realDeps`.

Tests. tests/mc/run-plan.test.js: `quotaResetAt` for the logged string with `now = 2026-09-08T09:05:00Z` → `2026-09-11T13:00:00.000Z`; `resets 3pm (Europe/Stockholm)` at 2026-09-08T09:05Z → same day 13:00Z, and at 14:00Z → next day; `resets Jan 2 at 9:30am (America/New_York)` from 2026-12-30 → 2027-01-02T14:30Z; garbage and an unknown zone → null. tests/mc/run.test.js: a session result with the logged text makes the recorded sleeps sum to the deadline and no session starts before it; a STOP file appearing after the first slice ends the pause.
docs/technical/mc-run.md: the quota paragraph (`grep -n -i "quota" docs/technical/mc-run.md`). Changelog entry.

steps.title: A process that hangs after its result is not a stalled step
steps.done_when: Once `streamSession` has seen the `result` line, the process gets `RESULT_GRACE_MS` (two minutes) to exit and is then killed with the result standing: status 0, `stalled: false`, and the `runs.tsv` note is the session's own word.
instruction: src/mc/run.js `streamSession`: the stall timer is re-armed on every stdout chunk and outlives the `result` on purpose. On 2026-09-13 `sql-w2-search-closure` finished (`"type":"result"`, `subtype: success`, 72.7 min) and its process then sat twenty minutes without exiting; the stall guard killed it, the run was logged `142 … stalled,failed`, and the reason read `the session ended stalled (rc 142) without landing it` — as if the session had never finished. The lane was also held twenty minutes for nothing.

Change: in `onResultLine`, after closing stdin, clear the stall timer and arm one `setTimeout` of `RESULT_GRACE_MS` (export `RESULT_GRACE_MS = 2 * 60 * 1000` from run-plan.js beside `DEFAULT_STALL_MINUTES`, and let `streamSession` take `resultGraceMs` as an option defaulting to it, so a test can pass 10). It is armed whether or not `stallMs` is set. `armStall` returns at once when `resultSeen` is true, so later chunks do not move it. When it fires: set a new flag `lingered = true`, `stop()`, `child.kill('SIGTERM')` — `stalled` stays false. On `close`: `status: stalled ? TIMEOUT_EXIT : (lingered ? 0 : (status ?? 1))`, `timedOut: stalled`, `stalled`, and add `lingered` to the resolved object. `stop()` clears this timer too.
The result line is only scanned for when the prompt is piped (`piped`), which is every step session; an unpiped session keeps today's behaviour exactly.

Nothing in the judgement after the session changes (run.js near line 1660): a step still `running` in the register is `failed` by ruling 21 — but its note is now `success,failed` and its reason `#N is open and the session ended success (rc 0) without landing it`, which is what happened. When `result.lingered`, add one `say` line: `<name>: the process did not exit within 2m of its result — killed, the result stands`.

tests/mc/run.test.js has `streamSession` cases with a fake `spawn` (`grep -n "streamSession" tests/mc/run.test.js`). Add: a child that writes a result line and never closes → killed after `resultGraceMs`, resolves `status: 0, stalled: false, lingered: true` and the stdout still holds the result; a child that writes chunks after the result does not extend the grace; a child that never writes a result still stalls with 142 as today.

docs/technical/mc-run.md: the sentence near line 908 (`It is armed at spawn and outlives the result`) becomes what is true now, and the sentence near line 575 about `stalled,open … which is then held` is removed — no code produces `stalled,open` and nothing is held (ruling 21). Changelog entry.

steps.title: mc status reads a killed merge the way the runner does
steps.done_when: `machineState` answers runnable for a worktree whose only dirt is a merge of origin/main left in progress, keeps `dirty` when there is other work beside it, and the `RUN_REFUSALS` agreement table has both cases.
instruction: `runStepClaimed` (src/mc/run.js near line 1415) runs `git merge --abort` when `MERGE_HEAD` exists, then does its dirty check. `machineState` in src/mc/status-collect.js was not taught that: `dirtyWorktree` reads the merge's rows as `a merge stopped in <path>: …`, reason `dirty`, so the page's NEXT and `mc status <name>` say the project waits on a person while the lane would abort the merge and run it.

A merge in progress does not only leave unmerged rows: every file main changed is staged (`M `, `A `, `D ` — a letter in the first column, a blank second). What a person or a session left beside the merge has a non-blank second column (` M`, `MM`, `AM`, ` D`) or is untracked (`??`). Unmerged rows are the seven codes in `UNMERGED`.

In `machineState`, before `dirtyWorktree` is called: `const merging = git(worktree, ['rev-parse', '-q', '--verify', 'MERGE_HEAD']).ok` — a read-only question, which this module's rule allows. When `merging`, read the porcelain rows with the two status columns kept as written (the existing row parser trims them; parse `line.slice(0, 2)` before trimming) and call the worktree clean when every row is either `UNMERGED` or has a blank second column and is not `??`. Otherwise — and whenever `MERGE_HEAD` is absent — `dirtyWorktree` answers as today. Do not run `merge --abort` here; this module reads.

tests/mc/run.test.js, the `RUN_REFUSALS` agreement table (`grep -n "RUN_REFUSALS" tests/mc/run.test.js`): add a case with `MERGE_HEAD` present and rows `UU a.js`, `M  b.js` → the runner starts the step and `machineState` says runnable; and one with the same plus ` M c.js` → both say `dirty`. tests/mc/status-collect.test.js: the two readings directly, and that the porcelain's leading-space rows are parsed by column (` M c.js` as first line — the git fake must not trim it).
docs/technical/mc-status.md where `dirty` is described. Changelog entry.
